transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (CTO - Apollo), Rachel Ng (Head of ML), Daniel Brooks (SRE)

Auto summary (auto-generated):
Apollo is evaluating migration from OpenAI-hosted inference to a Redwood Dedicated deployment for cost predictability and data isolation. Main drivers: token cost at scale, desire for private networking/VPC, and parity with current OpenAI outputs/finetune/evals. They are also running some on-prem tests with vLLM/TGI. Key concerns: eval parity, latency targets for user-facing features, security (SOC2, KMS/HSM), and rollout safety. Next steps: pricing, security docs, benchmark run.

Topics:
- Current stack and costs
- Compatibility and eval parity (OpenAI -> Redwood model variants)
- Performance: latency, batching, KV cache, quantization
- Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs
- Pilot/benchmark plan and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time today, I think we have about 45, 50 minutes on the calendar, great to meet you all. I'm Lena, AE on the account, and Marcus is our SE who will do the technical deep dive.
[00:12] Marcus: hi all, thanks for having us, quick agenda, we'll run through current infra, migration concerns, then talk compatibility and benchmarking.
[00:18] Samir: yep, thanks, quick context, we're Apollo Analytics, we run a question/answer product embedded in our dashboard, currently using OpenAI for generation, some parts run through vLLM on our infra for cost reasons. We're looking at Dedicated because costs are spinning up and we need more control around data.
[00:34] Rachel: and from ML side we care about eval parity, like the new outputs must match our existing test-suite, we have a battery of prompts and golden outputs.
[00:42] Daniel: SRE here, mostly concerned about networking, egress, and whether we can avoid sending PII out to third party clouds.
[00:50] Lena: makes sense. quick qual question, what's your current monthly token spend with OpenAI? ballpark?
[00:56] Samir: roughly $120k a month across chat and embeddings, embeddings are a big chunk.
[01:05] Marcus: ok that number definitely maps onto where Dedicated/reserved capacity starts to make sense. are you doing any finetuning or are you mostly using prompt engineering and few-shot?
[01:15] Rachel: mostly prompt engineering; we do a small amount of finetune-like re-ranking internally but not public finetunes on OpenAI.
[01:22] Marcus: good, that simplifies model parity. can you describe the models you use? GPT-4-ish family via OpenAI and for some throughput tests we run a 70B on vLLM/TGI locally.
[01:32] Samir: yes exactly, and for latency sensitive UI features we try to hit < 200ms generation latency for small completions.
[01:40] Lena: ok, bandwidth for the call, we'll outline Dedicated sizing and show what parity looks like. quick note on Hosted—if you'd rather keep the simplicity, our Hosted API can be used as drop-in, but it doesn't give the same isolation or committed throughput as Dedicated.
[01:55] Rachel: do you support the same API surface as OpenAI? we'd like minimal code changes.
[02:02] Marcus: we aim to be highly compatible; our SDK maps to the same request/response shapes for chat and completions and embeddings. there are some differences around streaming and function-calling semantics depending on the model, and of course model names differ. part of the pilot is to validate eval parity.
[02:20] Daniel: what's the workflow for private deployment? we may need VPC with customer-managed routing and KMS in our cloud.
[02:27] Lena: for Private we offer a customer-controlled control plane, can be deployed in your VPC or on-prem. KMS integration and HSM options are available - Marcus will share the security pack.
[02:40] Marcus: short on compatibility: we onboard open models and validate with our eval harness. many customers use our Dedicated infra with models that are compatible with GPT-style prompts. for vLLM/TGI users we typically recommend bringing your model weights and we handle kernel/quantization tuning. but if you rely on exact OpenAI logits for regen parity, we do an eval-run to show differences.
[02:59] Samir: okay, so regen parity—how different are outputs typically? do you have examples?
[03:06] Marcus: depends. if you're on a hosted proprietary OpenAI model, there's model mismatch. for most prompt-style tasks, our curated open models or Redwood-verified builds hit parity within acceptable bounds. for strict determinism we do an evaluation: run the same prompts, measure BLEU/ROUGE/our own task metrics and look at drift. we also recommend a canary rollout and a flag to fall back to the previous provider during the pilot.
[03:36] Rachel: and what about embeddings? we can't afford a big drift there.
[03:41] Marcus: embeddings are a bit trickier. we provide mapped embedding models and will compute cosine similarity on your reference pairs during the benchmark. sometimes customers re-index after migration; sometimes a small mapping layer fixes similarities. we'll include an embedding parity check in the benchmark template.
[03:58] Samir: networking question - we run in AWS. can Redwood Dedicated sit in our VPC or do we route traffic via Redwood edge?
[04:06] Marcus: Dedicated can be run as Dedicated-hosted in our clouds with private peering, or we can do a Private VPC deployment where the control plane is customer-managed. For strict data residency you can choose our Private package and we can deploy to your account, that's the typical pattern for regulated customers.
[04:27] Daniel: and egress - we need to ensure no PII leaves our VPC in plaintext.
[04:32] Marcus: we support per-customer encryption at rest and in transit, and KMS integration. for air-gapped needs we provide an on-prem package, but that requires a deeper infra engagement.
[04:44] Samir: performance - you mentioned batching and KV cache earlier. our UI is latency-sensitive, can you describe typical tail latency numbers?
[04:52] Marcus: baseline numbers depend on model and seq length. for typical 2-4 token completions on a 7B/13B style model we can be in the 50-120ms range on our Dedicated A100 pools with continuous batching. for 70B and above, expect higher latencies but we use KV cache and optimized kernels to keep interactive latencies low. if your SLO is <200ms that's feasible with a dedicated pool and correctly tuned batching/cold warm strategies.
[05:23] Rachel: what's the impact of quantization on our accuracy? we want to save cost but not degrade our eval metrics.
[05:29] Marcus: quantization depends on model family; 4-bit and 8-bit options can reduce GPU memory and allow denser packing. we run a recommendation pass in Redwood Optimize and show expected metric deltas on your eval set. some customers accept minor drops for huge cost savings; others prefer high fidelity.
[05:45] Lena: can we talk about rollout and safety? we recommend canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full, with automated rollback on quality regression.
[05:55] Marcus: we have per-prompt eval monitors and a canary policy that will fallback to Hosted/OpenAI if metrics drop. it's configurable.
[06:05] Samir: great. now about bench runs, how long do they usually take? we want to test embedding parity and regen parity and latency.
[06:12] Marcus: typical benchmark is 1 day for a representative sweep: regen parity on your golden set, embeddings similarity check, and a throughput run for your average and p95 seq lengths. we'll need your eval prompts and a traffic profile.
[06:25] Rachel: ok we'll give you the eval set, about 10k prompts, varied.
[06:29] Marcus: perfect. please also include 1k high-latency worst-case prompts.
[06:34] Daniel: on the procurement side, what's the contract cadence for Dedicated reserved capacity?
[06:39] Lena: we offer monthly reserved or annual commitments with discounts. Dedicated has capacity tiers; you can burst up if needed. pricing matrix gets sent after this call.
[06:49] Samir: any legal concerns? standard SOC2 plus HIPAA? Some of our customers require HIPAA.
[06:56] Marcus: we have SOC2 Type II and can support HIPAA under our Private/on-prem contract. we'll share the compliance pack - it lists audit logs, retention, and redaction options.
[07:08] Rachel: how does the eval harness run - do you run it inside our VPC or do we share artifacts?
[07:14] Marcus: we can run the benchmark in your VPC for Private deployments; for Dedicated hosted we'll run it in a dedicated account with no persistent storage and we can share the results and artifacts.
[07:26] Samir: curious about cost math - if we move embeddings to Dedicated, what percent cost reduction do customers typically see?
[07:33] Marcus: varies, but 30-60% is common once you're on reserved capacity and using batching/kv cache and optimized kernels. embeddings can be cheaper on CPU for certain throughput profiles, but on Dedicated GPUs with batching it's often best.
[07:48] Daniel: we currently run some embeddings on vLLM/TGI locally; would Redwood accept our vLLM models or weights for on-prem?
[07:56] Marcus: yes, bringing your weights is supported for Private and Dedicated on-prem. we handle kernel and quantization tuning to maximize throughput while preserving parity. note that TGI/vLLM runtime differences mean we'll still do an eval pass.
[08:12] Rachel: any red flags around license for model weights if they're community models?
[08:16] Marcus: legal side aside, technically we can host community models; license compliance is something we ask to confirm, we'll involve our legal teams as needed.
[08:26] Samir: can you run a quick sketch of the pilot timeline?
[08:30] Lena: typical pilot: week 0 we align on evals and traffic, week 1 run bench and parity tests, week 2 analyze and iterate on model config, week 3 canary rollout for small percent of production traffic. total 3-4 weeks for a conservative plan.
[08:47] Rachel: for the bench, what metrics will you return? we need token-level cost, latency percentiles, embedding cosine distributions, and regression deltas on our metrics.
[08:58] Marcus: yes, we'll provide a bench report with token-level cost breakdown, p50/p90/p99 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, embedding similarity histograms, and example output diffs.
[09:11] Daniel: logging/audit - do you provide per-request audit logs with masked PII?
[09:16] Marcus: yes, audit logs are available and we have redaction pipelines; for Private deployments you can route logs to your SIEM.
[09:24] Samir: anything about function calling support? we depend on structured outputs for some features.
[09:30] Marcus: function-calling is supported, semantics are largely compatible but again we'll validate the exact shape in the pilot. streaming and chunking behavior can differ by model.
[09:41] Rachel: what about model versioning and rollbacks?
[09:44] Marcus: Redwood has model version pins and rollout policies - you can pin a version per-route and do canary or A/B. automatic fallback is supported.
[09:52] Samir: sounds good. procurement wise, I will own approvals but Rachel and Daniel will sign off on perf and security.
[09:59] Lena: perfect. any other technical blocker?
[10:03] Daniel: firewall rules and peering - we might need a private link; what's required from our side?
[10:09] Marcus: we'll provide a network diagram and required ports; typically you need to allow peering and configure route tables. we'll add that to the security deck.
[10:19] Samir: curious if Redwood has run migrations from OpenAI at this scale before?
[10:24] Lena: yes, several customers in fintech and healthcare; we can share anonymized case studies and a reference architecture.
[10:31] Rachel: ok, technical ask - can you capture tokenization differences across models? we have fuzziness in tokens that shifts costs.
[10:39] Marcus: absolutely, tokenization and seq length calc is part of the bench - we'll report effective token counts and cost per hundred tokens mapping.
[10:47] Samir: for the bench we also want to check extremal tail cases - like long context and large batch embedding spikes.
[10:53] Marcus: we'll include stress tests and check autoscaling behavior for Dedicated.
[10:58] Lena: i'll summarize next steps: we'll send pricing and security docs, Marcus will send benchmark template, you send eval prompts and traffic profile, and we'll target a bench run next week.
[11:07] Samir: agree. I think we should do the bench in your Dedicated environment first to see parity before moving to Private.
[11:13] Rachel: yep that works.
[11:16] Daniel: ok, action items captured.
[11:19] Lena: any last questions?
[11:22] Samir: none from me. thanks.
[11:25] Marcus: cool, we'll follow up with the artifacts, expect email with attachments within 48 hours.
[56:30] -- call end --
